scope: Quest execution, event wiring, reserved mail, conditions, party objectives and progress persistence
implemented: All QuestType values 0..20 now have dispatch behavior; SendPost no longer falls through to child execution without sending anything.

SendPost shares the existing C# reward builder: normal/magic items, class masks, stack splitting, default/probability/random methods; no client-selected reward. Preserve the earlier C# exactly-one random reward and magic-prototype fixes.

Map commits all reserved attachments atomically with TQTITLECHART text and the native length-prefixed encoding. Grade effect, magic/value/ext slots, gem and appearance survive reservation and delivery. Children run only after successful reservation.

World drains up to 30 reserved posts per minute through native TGetReservedPost, including offline recipients. A transaction and database application lock protect concurrent .NET consumers; verify the header and attachment before committing, and set the mailbox attachment flag. Notify the recipient's current main.

Client requests cannot directly invoke server-event SendPost templates. Pending jobs are deduplicated within one event; DB failures do not run children or receive blind retries after ambiguous commits.

Position, level-up and map-leave triggers are wired into their existing events. The level event retains native previous-level chart keys; teleport uses the old map ID, and awaited logout mail/children precede the existing save/removal path.
Country conditions use war allegiance. Quest drops stop when their corresponding parent fetch objective is satisfied, even if another objective remains incomplete.
Quest EXP applies SDT_STATUS_QUESTEXP with saturation. The existing cap, soul-bar and level-up healing remain intact.

Native Regen kill triggers with MONID terms run once per local main party loop, in character-ID order; ordinary hunts still advance every member. Secondary reward routes retain the native separate branch.
Type-21 instance objectives resolve same-map/channel monsters and spawn-anchor proximity strictly below 16 units. Per-quest increments do not leak across different active quests.
Regen uses the event's death coordinates even when the original corpse exists only on a different Map server.
Recursive quest graphs have cycle/depth protection. Quest header and term saves commit in one transaction, preventing partial progress after a SQL failure.

Timed missions now distinguish an active timer from tick zero: accepting at server tick 0 persists and expires correctly; zero remaining after reload stays timed; abandonment/completion clear it and reacceptance starts a fresh timer. The existing strict greater-than expiry boundary is retained.

SendPost now atomically reserves attachments and updates its completed TQUESTTABLE counter under row/range locks. CountMax is enforced by both current memory and durable SQL, including concurrent Map instances and a newly loaded character. Already-issued results synchronize memory without replaying children; failed transactions consume neither rewards nor eligibility.

The loaded chart has 19 level-mail templates with CountMax=1 and 16 TT_WARREGION templates with CountMax=0. No chart limits or unrelated castle/fort/mission mail paths were changed. Uncapped counters remain repeatable across byte rollover.

GiveSkill now shares the earlier C# RT_SKILL level-zero activation fix. Existing learned skills stay unchanged, class/zero-max gates remain and only a newly activated skill runs children. UpdateSkill itself retains its existing add-only contract.
Dropping and reaccepting a type-21 objective clears its counter alongside hunt/talk/use-item counters, preventing retained progress from completing a new acceptance.

Successful single/take-all/lottery pickups now fire GETITEM objectives and acquisition triggers; destroying items refreshes counts without a new-acquisition event. Take-all respects lottery routing and only an in-game main recipient may receive items or quest credit.

Server ticks now enforce timer failure without client cooperation. Early/repeated timer-end requests cannot disable a deadline; failed zero-time reloads are immediate. Repeated active-timer saves and login packets use current remaining time. See Gameforge/quest-events.json for source/history and regressions.

Required quest-state loads now deny admission on failure instead of allowing an empty log. Headers and term counters read in one serializable transaction; both client/world entry paths reject failed loads. See Gameforge/quest-admission.json.

history_review.retained: Existing C# skill/reward prevalidation, ingredient preservation on failure, NPC dialog identity/country checks, repeatable craft behavior, one-random-reward rule and progression protections remain covered by the full suite.
history_review.deliberate_integrity_changes: Do not copy native partial item-by-item mail commits, ignored attachment-save errors, missing attachment properties or immediate child execution before DB success. Block direct client invocation of server-only mail events. SendPost now records completed progress, which the native implementation omitted despite consulting CanRunQuest/CountMax. No new cap values are introduced. Type-21 drop reset extends the existing counting-objective reset to an already-supported counting term.

validation.platform: Linux .NET 10 SDK, read-only source mounts; general database smoke suites run without live SQL credentials.
validation.isolated_database: 4DevQuestTest_20261030Events; empty storage table shapes/native procedures, synthetic character and text fixtures only.
validation.observed_existing_test_flake: The first run hit the unchanged CashShopTests.ACashBonusItem_GivesItsValueToTheBonus fire-and-forget DB-lane race. Subsequent full runs passed; cash-shop production logic and its tests were not changed.
validation.world_suite_note: World source is unchanged in the follow-up; its last full suite passed 207 tests, and its delivery data assembly also passes the expanded SQL scenarios.

remaining: Sixteen SendPost templates use TT_WARREGION (13). No producer of this event exists in the supplied C++ or C# server/client source. Do not invent the region-event rule; these templates do not yet run automatically.

SendPost character/mail continuations now have a durable SQL outbox, journaled issuance IDs and child-result receipts, including nested/sibling mail and uncapped same-ID replay. Process/file/SQL fault recovery is verified in Gameforge/quest-mail-recovery.json. External world effects remain explicitly pending/blocked, cross-Map ownership and general incoming-event identity remain open; do not claim universal exactly-once gameplay.

Durable whole-character and item retry is implemented and fault/process-tested for the current single-Map domain, including the full native/global/pet/companion callback. Quest event checkpoints now have synthetic interpreter/SQL process-exit recovery coverage; full MapWorker/client restart acceptance and cross-Map owner fencing remain open. See Gameforge/quest-checkpoints.json and quest-save-recovery.json. The legacy term-table key still excludes type; no term-ID/type collision occurs in loaded charts.
QCT_MONID and RT_CHGCLASS/TITLE have no functional native handler to port. Unused action metadata is not treated as an invented objective.

Full real-client acceptance, hunt/talk/use-item, timed failure, abandonment/reacceptance, turn-in choices, mailed rewards, quest chains, logout, restart and distributed topology remain acceptance gates. The pinned client's exact release and official content/balance parity are not certified.

current_deployment.note: Earlier implementation/validation notes retain their historical scope. Current cumulative source is deployed; deployment does not certify whole-game or full gameplay restart parity.
